task.title: rle-encode
task.statement: The rle package exposes decode (already implemented) and a stub encode(s). Implement encode(s) so that it run-length encodes a string: each maximal run of one character becomes that character followed by the decimal count of the run (the count is always written, even when it is 1). For example encode('aaabbc') is 'a3b2c1', encode('abc') is 'a1b1c1', encode('') is ''. encode must return a str and must round-trip with decode (decode(encode(x)) == x for every string x). Raise TypeError when s is not a string. Do not change decode or the tests.
acceptance_criteria: TypeError when s is not a string

spec.restated_task: Implement the `encode` function in the `rle` package to perform run-length encoding on a string. Each maximal run of identical characters is replaced by the character followed by its decimal count (always written, even for a count of 1). The function must return a string, raise `TypeError` for non-string inputs, and satisfy the round-trip property `decode(encode(x)) == x` for all strings `x`. The existing `decode` function and tests must remain unchanged.

interface_contract.name: encode
interface_contract.behavior: Returns the run-length encoding of the input string `s`. Each maximal run of a single character is represented as that character followed by the decimal count of the run (the count is always written, even when it is 1). For example, `encode('aaabbc')` returns `'a3b2c1'`, `encode('abc')` returns `'a1b1c1'`, `encode('')` returns `''`.
error_cases: TypeError: raised when `s` is not a string.

interface_contract.name: decode
interface_contract.behavior: Decodes a run-length encoded string `s` back to the original string. The input must consist of a character followed by one or more digits for each run. For example, `decode('a3b1')` returns `'aaab'`, `decode('')` returns `''`.
error_cases: TypeError: raised when `s` is not a string.
ValueError: raised when a character is not followed by at least one digit (missing count).

acceptance_criteria: decode(encode(x)) == x for every string x (round-trip property)
encode raises TypeError when the argument is not a string (e.g., encode(123) raises TypeError)
The existing decode function behavior is unchanged: decode('a3b1') == 'aaab', decode('') == '', and decode(123) raises TypeError
encode handles strings with multiple runs of the same character separated by other characters (e.g., encode('aaabba') == 'a3b2a1')
out_of_scope: The implementer must not modify the `decode` function.
The implementer must not modify the existing test file `tests/test_basic.py`.
The implementer must not change the public function signatures (i.e., `encode` must accept a single argument and return a string).
The implementer must not add any external dependencies.

sealed_tests.notes: All acceptance criteria covered with dedicated test methods; round-trip verified across varied inputs.
